items.text: An AI-led selloff hit Wall Street on Friday, Nov 20. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to about 6,910, its seventh straight loss, and the Dow fell 1.9% (950 points) to 48,147. Both are now more than 10% below their records, which puts them in correction. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3% to 22,618 and is now down for 2026. Reuters says Anthropic's IPO fell flat, which deepened worries about the AI trade, and Nvidia's strong results did not calm fears about heavy AI spending. Nvidia fell about 14%, AMD, Micron and Broadcom each lost 12–14%, and tech was the worst sector (-7.3%). The S&P lost 8.6% on the week, its worst week since April 2025. The VIX jumped to about 36, Treasury yields fell sharply (10-year 4.92%), gold dropped about 4.6%, and bitcoin fell below $60,000. Asian chip-heavy markets had already fallen 5–6%.
items.notes: Small differences between sources: Reuters has Nvidia -13.8% and Anthropic -9.1%; the Capp Notes wrap has -14.01% and -8.50% (Anthropic closed at $88.91, still above its $83 IPO price). Sector, VIX, yield and commodity figures come only from the Capp Notes wrap.

items.text: At a long White House news conference on Nov 20, Trump said he would 'love to see' Jensen Huang 'given a second chance' as Nvidia CEO. He called Huang a good man who made bad decisions and urged him to apologise and return. Trump also said Xi Jinping had called Huang 'brilliant' during their Shenzhen meeting. Al Jazeera notes this contradicts Treasury Secretary Bessent's account that Huang did not come up. Nvidia's board, led by chair Harvey Jones, has said it unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and does not plan to reinstate him. Trump said he still backs Commerce Secretary Lutnick, whom Sen. Tom Cotton accuses of ignoring warnings about chip smuggling to China. Democrats are looking into whether Lutnick helped Cantor Fitzgerald.
items.notes: Trump's account of Xi's remark conflicts with Bessent's, per Al Jazeera. No board response to Trump found as of Nov 21.

items.text: At the same Nov 20 news conference, Trump said US companies that build data centres in other countries would face 'tremendous penalties' or 'a tremendous tax'. He argued that 'China will take all of them' and framed the threat as part of an AI race with China. He gave no details on how a penalty would work or on its legal basis. He also said he and Xi had agreed on unspecified 'joint guardrails' for AI. US cloud and AI companies, including hyperscalers and OpenAI, are building large data-centre projects abroad, especially in the Gulf, Europe and Southeast Asia. The threat follows the Nov 19 BIS rule requiring licences for advanced chips in data centres in several Southeast Asian countries.
items.notes: A verbal threat; no executive action found. The CNBC article could not be fetched, so only the headline was seen. No company reaction found yet.

items.text: On Nov 20 Trump signed an executive order requiring federal contractors and subcontractors to notify the White House and their contracting agencies about any pending or future congressional request concerning their government work or their communications with the executive branch. They must coordinate on responses and on which privileges apply, and must withhold material the White House says is covered by executive privilege. Agencies must tell contractors about these duties. The White House says the order protects confidential and national-security information. Reuters notes that Democrats take control of both chambers in January and are expected to launch investigations of the administration. Oversight experts expect the order to be contested, but no reactions were found yet.
items.notes: The line about experts expecting a challenge is analysis, not sourced reaction. The Reuters piece quotes no lawmakers. The EO number was not confirmed.

items.text: Late on Nov 19 the Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), a broad permitting overhaul, by 62-33. Fifteen Democrats joined almost all Republicans. Thirty-one Democrats and Republicans Hawley and Rounds voted no. The bill changes how reviews and permits work under NEPA, the Endangered Species Act, the Clean Water Act, the Historic Preservation Act and the Federal Power Act. It limits lawsuits against projects, gives FERC new authority over interstate transmission lines, and includes provisions meant to keep ordinary ratepayers from paying for power hookups to data centres. The White House backs it, and Trump claimed on Nov 20 that it would save households $1,300 a year. The Sierra Club, NRDC, 17 Democratic states and tribal groups oppose it. It goes to the House after Thanksgiving. Speaker Johnson says it can pass, but Jeffries' office says it 'falls short'.
items.notes: The vote was late on Nov 19 ET and was not in the earlier logs. Trump's $1,300 savings figure is his claim (CBS live blog). Wyden's proposed amendment banning data centres on public lands: outcome not reported.

items.text: Fed officials kept signalling a December rate hike. According to a Nov 20 market wrap, Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson, a 2026 voter, said she would be open to back-to-back hikes, and Governor Lisa Cook warned that waiting longer risks falling behind the curve. Cook dissented against hiking in October. Kalshi priced a 25bp hike at the Dec 8–9 FOMC meeting at about 90%. Data released the same day were softer: the University of Michigan's final November survey showed one-year inflation expectations falling to 3.7% from 4.3% at mid-month, the lowest since March, and sentiment at 51.5. Treasury yields fell 12–13bp as investors sought safety.
items.notes: The Cook and Paulson Nov 20 remarks were not confirmed in a primary Fed transcript; the Investinglive Paulson piece may be from earlier in the week. Relevant to W-261107-01.

items.text: A Nov 20 market wrap says Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are examining Nvidia's accounting, and that California Attorney General Rob Bonta's office sent Nvidia an investigative subpoena over whether its chips reached China. Both were cited as reasons for the stock's roughly 14% fall. Earlier, the WSJ (Nov 17) reported a civil SEC probe into whether Nvidia's disclosures about Asia misled investors, including its ties to Singapore's Megaspeed. Bonta had told Bloomberg TV that 'red flags' had been raised and that he was weighing action.
items.notes: The subpoena and accounting-focus details were not seen in a primary Reuters or AG source; treat with caution. The SEC disclosure probe itself was reported by the WSJ on Nov 17.

items.text: In his first news conference since the midterms, back from Asia, Trump said he would veto Democratic-led bills unless Democrats work with him and would issue an 'ultimatum' later. He said he is open to working with them on healthcare, called Hakeem Jeffries 'a smart guy', and described a productive call with Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa. He brought his new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, to the lectern and asked him whether he wants to run for president. He defended Vance's remark blaming the Iran war for GOP midterm losses and said he would have won had he been on the ballot. He did not lay out a plan for the Dec 11 funding deadline.
items.notes: The CNN takeaways page could not be read (robots block), so only its headline was seen. CBS did not cover funding or shutdown remarks.

items.text: Trump said at his Nov 20 news conference that National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving and that Kirsten Davies has been named to replace him, pending Senate confirmation. He also said the recent string of outages, including the FAA ground stop and the NSANet disruption, were 'all separate events'. Cairncross was confirmed in August 2025. The change comes as senators press the White House over AI-enabled cyber threats.
items.notes: Only the CBS live blog was seen; no official announcement or independent confirmation of Davies' nomination was found. Relevant to W-261118-02 and W-261114-01.

items.text: Trump said he met more than 20 leaders on his Asia trip, 'secured two new trade deals' and expects about ten more 'very soon'. He named neither deal. He said the US is 'getting close to a deal' with Mexico and working with it against cartels, and that Canada has been 'ripping us off' and is not yet satisfactory. Earlier, the Philippine ambassador said nothing had been signed with Manila despite Trump's claim of the 'biggest trade deal' ever.
items.notes: No deal texts were found. These are Trump's claims.

items.text: Trump defended his relationship with Vladimir Putin on Nov 20. He said Putin told him the Ukraine war would never have happened had Trump been president, and that the relationship gives the US 'additional strength'. Russia launched more attacks on Ukraine after the Shenzhen meetings. Trump said the joint statement with Xi and Putin covered non-proliferation, refined-petroleum supply, rejecting ICC authority and UN reform. On Iran, he said there is a 'rumor' Tehran is building a dirty bomb, which the US 'will not allow', and that he wants a 'real deal', not a 'fake' one. He also touted an almost 60-cent drop in average gasoline prices over the past month.
items.notes: The dirty-bomb allegation first surfaced around Nov 17 and Iran denied it. The gas-price figure is Trump's claim.

items.text: US District Judge Charlotte Sweeney in Colorado held ICE officials and the administration in contempt for repeatedly re-arresting immigrants immediately after courts ordered their release, a practice the ACLU calls 'sham releases', Democracy Now reported on Nov 20. The central case involves Ramón Quintero Álvarez, a Mexican immigrant who has lived in the US for more than 30 years and was re-arrested right after leaving the Aurora ICE detention centre in late October. Any sanctions were not detailed.
items.notes: Only one outlet seen (left-leaning). Ruling date and penalties not confirmed.

items.text: On Nov 20 US District Judge Vernon Oliver, a Biden appointee, preliminarily blocked four sections of Connecticut's 2026 law SB 397. The sections would have let the state Inspector General investigate and criminally prosecute federal agents and made it a misdemeanour for officers to wear face coverings while dealing with the public. He found the provisions likely violate the Supremacy Clause because they impose conditions and penalties on federal officers, and said the Justice Department, which sued in May, is likely to win. Courts have also blocked California's ban on masked federal agents.
items.notes: This is a preliminary injunction and the case continues.

items.text: The AP reports that the Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to let the EPA cancel about $16 billion in Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund 'green bank' grants created by the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act. In August a divided DC Circuit panel ruled the terminations unlawful, but release of the money was paused, under a deal with the grantees, to give the justices a chance to weigh in. The petition, filed this month (docket 26-589, Climate United Fund and other nonprofits as respondents), is on the regular docket, not the emergency docket. The justices have not said whether they will take the case.
items.notes: The petition appears to date from early November (a Climate United filing on the docket is dated Nov 2), but the AP story ran Nov 19 and SCOTUSblog covered it Nov 20. Sources give the amount as $16bn, $17bn or $20bn.

items.text: The FDA published a new web page and report on shellfish harvesting in federal waters, including a sanitary survey of the federal-waters portion of the San Pedro Shelf off southern California and a letter to NOAA about Seafood Inspection Program contracts for harvesters there. Separately, Grand Strand Sandwich Company recalled lunch-box sandwiches on Nov 19 over possible Listeria contamination. The FDA's outbreak table also updated entries for a romaine-linked Salmonella outbreak and two other Salmonella outbreaks.
items.notes: This is a routine digest. No new FDA commissioner nominee was found.

items.text: During a large Russian strike on western Ukraine overnight on Nov 19–20, three Russian objects entered Polish airspace and crashed in south-east Poland. A Kh-101 cruise missile fell in a field at Nowy Lipowiec (Biłgoraj county, Lublin region), about 200–300 m from houses. Another missile fell in forest near Rudnik nad Sanem, and what was probably a jet-powered drone fell at Mołodycz (Jarosław county, both Podkarpackie). Nobody was hurt. One roof was damaged, possibly by the blast wave. Gen. Ireneusz Nowak said 11 objects threatened Polish airspace and three crossed the border, at 6:29 and 6:34 according to the BBN. The Operational Command said fighters were cleared to fire, but the conditions for doing so were not met. Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz called it one of the largest such incidents since 2022. Prosecutors in Lublin are investigating.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: There was early confusion over Rudnik. The Podkarpackie voivode first described the falls at Rudnik and Mołodycz as unmanned aircraft, while the defence minister spoke of a missile at Rudnik (WP live blog). The early Notes from Poland report said only 'unidentified object', and the army at first called it a 'suspected' violation.

items.text: PM Donald Tusk said it was certain that what fell in Poland came from Russia, and that it looked like an intentional provocation, not an accident. He and Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz linked the timing to the coalition of the willing's KOALICJA 26.2 exercise at Nowa Dęba. Tusk spoke at length with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. Rutte called the violations clearly dangerous, said allied jets were scrambled, and said NATO will keep strengthening deterrence. He was due in Warsaw on Saturday, Nov 21. Kosiniak-Kamysz said he would ask NATO for extra forces for Eastern Sentry and for more surveillance and air defence. Macron, Czech President Pavel and Portugal expressed solidarity. No invocation of NATO Article 4 had been reported.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: The outcome of Rutte's Saturday visit was not yet reported when this was researched. No Russian official response was found. The BBN said President Nawrocki had been briefed since early morning, but no presidential statement was found. Right-wing outlets (wPolityce) ran pieces blaming the government over air defence; those articles could not be opened.

items.text: The incident raised questions about civilian warnings. Government spokesman Adam Szłapka said the RCB sent a first warning of a possible threat at 2:31. A phone alert went out at 6:30, sirens sounded in Nowy Lipowiec a minute later, and the missile fell at 6:36. Some residents said warnings arrived only after the explosion. Andrzej Borowiec, wójt of Aleksandrów, said his phone alert came seconds after the impact and that outlying villages need more sirens. He added that local officials get no earlier information than ordinary citizens. Tusk said he would check the timing of the sirens and alerts.
items.thread: Russian missiles and drones over Poland
items.notes: The right-wing portal prawy.pl reported, without corroboration found, that the Rzeszów-Jasionka control tower was evacuated and civil air traffic briefly halted. That claim is not included as fact.

items.text: President Karol Nawrocki appointed Finance Minister Andrzej Domański as deputy prime minister, the fourth in Donald Tusk's government, and appointed Agnieszka Bartol minister of funds and regional policy, at a ceremony in the Presidential Palace's Column Hall. He also dismissed Katarzyna Pełczyńska-Nałęcz, who left the government and Polska 2050 in October. Bartol, 54, is a career EU official and was Poland's ambassador to the EU. The appointments had been delayed for a month amid the President–government conflict. A presidential minister said that if it had been up to Nawrocki there would have been no promotion. Tusk wrote on X that both would work for Poland in their new roles.
items.notes: Resolves W-261105-07. Rzeczpospolita (Nov 17) described contradictory signals from the Chancellery beforehand (Bogucki vs spokesman Leśkiewicz).

items.text: Tusk said the Christmas wafer (opłatek) meeting he had proposed to President Nawrocki will not take place. He said the President had indicated they would probably not meet before the holidays and would send good wishes instead. On Nov 11 Tusk had publicly invited Nawrocki and his family to his flat in Sopot to talk 'like one Pole with another'.
items.notes: Based on Tusk's account; no Chancellery comment found.

items.text: A consortium led by FedEx completed its €7.8bn (34.5bn zł) takeover of InPost, Poland's parcel-locker and delivery company, at €15.60 a share. InPost was delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. FedEx and the US fund Advent each hold 37%, founder Rafał Brzoska's A&R Investments 16% and the Czech PPF 10%. InPost keeps its Polish headquarters, brand and operational independence, and Brzoska stays CEO. The deal was announced in February and cleared by the European Commission in August.
items.notes: No Polish government reaction reported.

items.text: The Military District Court in Warsaw overturned the acquittal of soldier Karol S. and sent his case back for retrial. He is charged with exceeding his powers by firing 12 warning shots at a group of migrants near Dubicze Cerkiewne on the Belarus border on March 25, 2024. The court said at least three shots put migrants, and fellow soldiers and Border Guard officers, at direct risk of death or serious injury. The charge carries up to three years in prison. The garrison court in Lublin had acquitted him.
items.notes: Politically sensitive: the right has campaigned for soldiers prosecuted over border incidents. No reaction found yet.

items.text: The Energy Minister set maximum fuel prices for Saturday to Monday (Nov 21–23): 5.90 zł a litre for 95 petrol, 6.55 zł for 98 petrol and 7.39 zł for diesel, under the daily price-cap scheme.
items.notes: Figures come from the WNP headline only. The article would not load, and the date (Nov 20) is inferred from the article ID sequence, so check it before relying on it.

items.text: The city has set the dates for public consultation on Mayor Łukasz Gibała's plan to shrink the Clean Transport Zone (SCT) from about 196 km² to about 0.99 km² in the city centre. KRKnews reports the consultation runs from 27 November to 18 December 2026. Residents can respond with an online form, available from 27 November, or on paper, or by phone through the Kraków Contact Centre (12 616 55 55). Experts will take calls on 4 and 11 December. Four open meetings, each 17:00–19:00, are planned: 3 December at ARTzona (os. Górali 4), 7 December at Rynek Podgórski 1, 10 December at XIV LO (ul. Chełmońskiego 24) and 17 December at the Sala Kupiecka on pl. Wszystkich Świętych. The separate consultation on freezing SCT fees for 2027–2028 still closes on 27 November.
items.notes: The dates come from KRKnews, which describes the city's announcement. The city's own communiqué was not seen directly.

items.text: City Hall has partly backed away from raising property tax in 2027. LoveKraków reports that the draft presented at the 18 November session keeps 2026 rates for flats and for 'other land' such as courtyards. The earlier plan was to raise them to the statutory maximum: 1.29 zł per m² for flats, 4 groszy more, and 80 groszy for other land, up from 77. The city had expected about 17m zł in extra revenue and now says it must find 3–4m zł elsewhere. A PiS amendment from Michał Ciechowski would have frozen only the rate for flats. Commercial rates still rise; the top rate for service buildings was 35.53 zł per m² in 2026. Michał Starobrat (Kraków dla Mieszkańców) said ordinary residents are spared. Michał Drewnicki (PiS) called the freeze a symbolic gesture and said City Hall should cut its own costs first.
items.thread: Kraków city finances and the 2027 budget
items.notes: The revised druk 1617 text was not seen on BIP. The amounts are LoveKraków's. Adoption comes at a later session.

items.text: Prosecutor Eryk Stasielak of the National Prosecutor's Office told PAP that the 7 November attacker fired an estimated 100+ shots in Kraków; the exact count is still being checked. CCTV has now been used to trace his route from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, with one stop on the way. He entered via al. Słowackiego, plac Biskupi and ul. Szczepańska, and his first shot, at Szczepańska and Sławkowska, killed a British citizen. He had a permit for 10 firearms but only two registered: an AR-15 and a Glock. Prosecutors will question witnesses, including doctors and psychologists, about how the permit was issued. They are asking people who were on ul. Grodzka to come forward, after videos showing shots near a child. The body has been released; RMF FM says a relative collected it. Toxicology results are pending. No motive has been stated. The voivode said five injured people remain in Kraków hospitals.
items.outlet: PAP via nczas.info; Kraków Portal; Krakowski Raport
items.notes: New since the 19 Nov log: CCTV route, the 10-firearm permit and the questioning about it, the Grodzka witness appeal, and the body being collected (RMF FM, per Krakowski Raport). The '5 still in hospital' figure is from the Małopolska voivode (Krakowski Raport digest).

items.text: Mayor Gibała has opened recruitment for three more posts. They are director of the Urban Planning Department (after the previous director was dismissed), plenipotentiary for senior policy, and plenipotentiary for violations of law, the 'legal violations envoy' announced earlier in November. Applications for all three close on 3 December. Qualifying tests are on 7 December (seniors), 8 December (planning) and 9 December (legal violations). The earlier competition for director of the Sports Infrastructure Authority (ZIS) closes on 29 November. The city says full terms are on BIP.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor

items.text: The board of the municipal holding Krakowski Holding Komunalny (KHK) has abolished the adviser post held by Szczęsny Filipiak, former head of Platforma Obywatelska in Kraków, LoveKraków reports. Filipiak confirmed it. Because he is a Małopolska regional assembly councillor, ending his employment needs the assembly's prior consent, and PiS holds the majority there. The article gives no reasons for the decision. KHK's supervisory board dismissed the whole management board, including Bogusław Kośmider, on 10 November. An interim board is running the company, and a competition for a permanent board is under way (applications 24 Nov, new board from January).
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: KRKnews (20 Nov) quotes Filipiak as the sharpest critic of Gibała's first month.

items.text: The Main Square Christmas market runs from 27 November 2026 to 1 January 2027, with about 100 stalls selling goods from Poland, Lithuania, Slovakia, Hungary, the UK and Ukraine. A separate fair on Mały Rynek opens on 30 November. Karta Krakowska holders get a 20% discount. LoveKraków says this may be the last market in its current form. The city's contract with the organiser, the Kraków Merchants' Congregation, ends after this season, and the options include a tender or the city taking over the event. Mayor Gibała has said organisers should be judged on looks and quality, not only money. Congregation president Wiesław Jopek urged visitors to return after the 7 November attack.

Rebuilding of ul. Witosa in Podgórze starts on 25 November at 10:00. The carriageway towards Kurdwanów narrows to one lane for about 250 m. The first section, between Halszki and the Beskidzka junction, adds a turnaround lane for drivers leaving Trasa Łagiewnicka towards Beskidzka, Malwowa and Gołaśka. It also replaces water and power networks, lighting and drainage and adds a pavement and bike path. Kurdwanów residents and Akcja Ratunkowa dla Krakowa had protested over tree felling. The revised design moves paths to spare greenery, transplants three trees and plans almost 200 replacement trees in Podgórze Duchackie. Completion is planned for July 2027.
items.notes: LoveKraków's lead says mid-2027 but its body says the end of July 2027. Neither outlet gives the cost or names the contractor.

items.text: GDDKiA plans to open the remaining connectors at the S7 Mistrzejowice interchange (Nowa Huta to S52, and the northern bypass to S7 towards Nowa Huta) around the turn of November and December. Links to Petöfiego and Okulickiego streets follow at the end of 2026. Traffic from Grębałów towards Warsaw will not use the main viaducts. It will join the northern-bypass connector, at first in one right-hand lane. Critics say this overloads a connector redesigned in 2022. GDDKiA spokesman Kacper Michna said there are no ideal solutions here. The main S7 carriageway over the viaducts opened on 30 October.

Kraków Batowice station has reopened after a rebuild. KRKnews reports four new platforms instead of two and a footbridge with lifts linking Szmaragdowa and Dziekanowicka streets. Track, switches and catenary have been replaced, allowing 120 km/h on the upgraded section of line 8. A local control centre at Batowice now runs digital signalling for Zastów, Niedźwiedź, Miechów, Słomniki, Tunel and Nowa Huta, and six level crossings were upgraded. The three linked projects on line 8 (Kraków Główny–Tunel), including platforms in Miechów, Smroków and Zastów, cost over 523m zł gross, funded from the EU Recovery Plan (KPO).
items.notes: No exact reopening date is given. The article was published 20 Nov.

items.text: Stalexport Autostrada Małopolska, which runs the toll A4 motorway between Katowice and Kraków, plans group layoffs. CoWKrakowie reports they would cover almost all staff except the management board, ahead of the concession's expiry on 15 March 2027. The parent company Stalexport Autostrady announced the plan. The article does not say who will take over toll collection or what tolls will be after the concession ends.
items.notes: Published 19 Nov at 12:58. Not in the logged events. No headcount is given.

items.text: Deputy Prime Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz (PSL) said in Jarosław on 19 November that his party backs a Kraków metro and will seek funding with Infrastructure Minister Dariusz Klimczak, while 'Kraków must make its contribution', Puls Krakowa reports. Mayor Gibała repeats that preparations stay suspended until the state or the EU gives binding guarantees. On 20 November political scientist Prof. Łukasz Danel told Radio Kraków that the metro dispute is the first serious clash between mayor and council and that pausing means abandoning the project. Deputy Mayor Wałachowski's analysis of money already spent is not yet published, and the geological-survey tender is still before the National Appeals Chamber (KIO). The extraordinary session is on 25 November at 16:00.
items.notes: Danel's remarks are analysis/opinion. The Kosiniak-Kamysz statement was 19 Nov afternoon and was not previously logged.

items.text: A tram on line 15 derailed on the morning of 20 November on ul. Kamienna, outside Dworzec Towarowy, while heading to Krowodrza Górka P+R. CoWKrakowie reports that trams towards Krowodrza Górka and Górka Narodowa were sent via ul. Długa, while those towards Rondo Mogilskie ran normally. No cause or reopening time was given.

Koleje Mazowieckie's seasonal 'Śnieżny' train from Warsaw to Zakopane will stop at Kraków Główny. It first runs on 17 December 2026, with extra runs in both directions on 24 and 27 December. After Kraków it calls at Skawina, Kalwaria Zebrzydowska, Lanckorona, Sucha Beskidzka Zamek, Maków Podhalański, Chabówka Stadion, Nowy Targ and Poronin. Warsaw–Kraków costs 55 zł full fare and Warsaw–Zakopane 70 zł. It uses double-deck carriages with 436–750 seats.

Football club Cracovia has a new management board: Piotr Sadczuk with supervisory board members Philip Platek and Marcin Stefaniak, who are delegated temporarily. KRKnews describes it as a transitional board. The club says the aim is stability and continuity of management. This follows weeks of turmoil at the club, including a coach change and a dispute with its former president. LoveKraków reports that a director was promoted to president.

Voivode Krzysztof Jan Klęczar attended the signing of agreements giving over 14m zł of government money to 11 Małopolska municipalities and counties. More than 10m zł from the Government Road Development Fund will rebuild over 5 km of local roads in Lipnica Wielka (Nowy Targ county), Kasina Wielka (Mszana Dolna), Czarna Góra (Bukowina Tatrzańska) and Ryglice (Tarnów county). More than 4m zł goes to repair flood and storm damage on about 7.5 km of roads and two culverts in Łapanów, Jodłownik, Trzciana, Ciężkowice, Gnojnik, Koniusza and Gołcza.
items.notes: The voivodeship office is the photo source. The official communiqué was not seen.

items.text: Jagiellonian University won the social sciences category of the Research Impact Leaders Awards 2026, announced on 19 November in Bydgoszcz at the KRASP plenary. The University of Warsaw and Adam Mickiewicz University were the other finalists. The UJ press office cites a 14% rise in publications, more than 2,800 papers in 2023–2025 (one in ten among the world's most cited) and international co-authorship on 30% of the assessed research.
items.notes: Kraków Portal's URL refers to Elsevier. The award's sponsor was not verified.

items.text: Kraków is one of 29 cities in WWF's 'We Love Cities 2026' campaign. Residents can vote and submit ideas free of charge on WWF's site until 30 November, or post with #WeLoveKrakow. Sample proposals include more trees, pocket parks, cyclist safety, heat adaptation and rainwater use. Kraków Portal notes the ideas go to the city but need not be funded, and that the campaign is not a rating of the city's environment.

KRKnews asked seven local politicians to assess Mayor Gibała's first month. KO senator Monika Piątkowska said a month is too short to judge. PiS council deputy chair Michał Drewnicki called it a good start. Razem's Aleksandra Owca said the mayor lacks a council majority and KO may block him. Regional councillor Szczęsny Filipiak accused him of skipping promised audits and competitions. Konfederacja's Bartosz Bocheńczak and Ruch Narodowy's Piotr Bartosz welcomed the smaller SCT but questioned the metro halt (Bocheńczak). Former councillor Łukasz Wańtuch gave a 4+ but criticised the Lviv move.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: These are opinions.

items.text: Cyclone Akvan, which crossed the coast near Gopalpur on the morning of Nov 20, caused no deaths and no major damage in Odisha, Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said (PTI via Business Standard). Chief Secretary Anu Garg put evacuations at about 3.7 lakh, with 423 rescue teams deployed. The heaviest rain fell in Ganjam district: Patrapur 209 mm, Hinjili 207 mm, Gopalpur 190 mm. TPSODL said it had restored supply to 10.69 lakh consumers (98.68%) within seven hours. By Nov 21 the system was a depression. Aaj Tak reports trees down in nine districts, waterlogging in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack, some landslides and 28 express trains cancelled, but the state says there is no flood threat. Neighbouring Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand ordered crop-loss surveys.
items.notes: Power figures from TPSODL via OdishaBytes (https://odishabytes.com/cyclone-akvan-tpsodl-restores-power-to-10-69-lakh-consumers-achieves-nearly-99-restoration-within-7-hours/). Crop-survey orders in CG/Jharkhand per Kisan India (https://www.kisanindia.in/agriculture-money/cyclone-akvan-crop-damage-compensation-farmers-chhattisgarh-jharkhand-odisha-170110.html). No AP RTGS damage figures found. Evacuation count differs: about 3.7 lakh (Chief Secretary) vs 2.99 lakh in camps (earlier Open Press figure).

items.text: Ladakh voted on Nov 21 in its first panchayat and municipal elections since it became a Union Territory, after an eight-year gap. Polling ran from 8 am to 5 pm across all eight districts. All 21 wards of the Leh Municipal Committee and 13 of 17 Kargil wards were contested. Of 192 panchayats, 55 sarpanches were elected unopposed, leaving 137 contests. Of 1,428 panch seats, 1,186 were filled unopposed. Counting is on Dec 4, the same day as polls for 100 seats on the eight hill councils. The Leh Apex Body has protested and wants the hill-council polls put off until 2027. Activist Sonam Wangchuk remains under a 60-day restriction order.
items.thread: Ladakh statehood protests and council polls
items.notes: Greater Kashmir gives 242 contested panch seats; Dainik Jagran (Nov 19) said about 212. Turnout not yet reported. Counting date of Dec 4 per Greater Kashmir.

items.text: PM Narendra Modi opened the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Qila, New Delhi, on Nov 20. The forum runs until Nov 22 and is organised by the Culture and External Affairs ministries in the SCO's 25th-anniversary year. India proposed it at the 2025 Tianjin summit. About 25 countries were invited, including all 10 SCO members, and Pakistan sent a minister. According to PIB summaries, India proposed joint digitisation and translation of ancient manuscripts (including with AI), shared-history research, museum exhibitions, scholar exchanges and Silk Route and Buddhist heritage circuits. Modi described cultural bonds as the strongest guarantee of peace.
items.notes: Proposal list from a PIB digest (https://www.legacyias.com/pib-summaries-21-november-2026/). The 'strongest guarantee for peace' line is from The Statesman's headline; the article itself could not be fetched.

items.text: Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik, the first Pakistani federal minister in India since 2023, is attending the SCO forum. The MEA's Randhir Jaiswal called it a multilateral event to which all members were invited. Asked about Malik's earlier Indus Waters Treaty remarks, Jaiswal said India's position has not changed (Aaj Tak). Hindi outlets report that the government refused Malik's requests to visit the Taj Mahal and Nizamuddin Dargah, citing security, and limited him to the Delhi event. No official statement confirms this. Asked by reporters whether culture can mend ties, Malik said it plays an important role. Patrika quotes him hoping visits between the two countries will continue. No bilateral meeting has been reported.
items.notes: The Taj/Nizamuddin refusal rests on media reports, not an official statement. Navbharat Live also says he sidestepped a question on terrorism. Patrika quote: https://www.patrika.com/national-news/musadik-malik-statement-india-visit-sco-dialogue-forum-21071773

items.text: At the MEA briefing on Nov 20, spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India had taken note of the ICJ's 9–6 ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. He said India supports the safe, speedy and sustainable return of displaced Rohingya. He rejected statements by the US Commission on International Religious Freedom about Indian voter rolls, calling the body biased and politically motivated. India will wait for concrete outcomes before assessing the Russia–China–US meeting in Shenzhen. On Qatar, India is seeking details of the health and recent hospitalisation of detained ex-Navy commander Purnendu Tiwari, who was sentenced there in February.
items.notes: The briefing also listed outcomes of the Quad summit in Manila.

items.text: SEBI has proposed scrapping the additional disclosures that higher-risk offshore funds must make, including on their ultimate beneficial owners, Bloomberg and IANS report. These rules mainly cover funds with concentrated holdings in Indian companies. They were tightened in 2023 after probes into overseas funds linked to Adani Group investments. SEBI says existing beneficial-ownership norms already give enough transparency, and that the extra rules are out of step with global practice and could put India at a competitive disadvantage. The proposal is open for public consultation. It comes as foreign portfolio investors put a record ₹84,291 crore into Indian equities in the first half of November.
items.notes: Consultation-paper number, thresholds and comment deadline not seen; the SEBI website listing could not be checked. FPI figure from Kotak Neo.

items.text: Indian shares rose for a second day on Nov 20, even after weak overnight Asian and US markets amid an AI-led tech sell-off. The Sensex closed at 83,919.71, up about 898 points (1.08%), and the Nifty at 25,800.60, up 1.12%, a nine-month high. Nifty Bank rose 2.49% and Nifty IT 1.30%, while metals and small caps slipped. Kotak Neo credits continued foreign buying. Foreign investors put a record ₹84,291 crore into Indian equities in the first half of November, and the rupee was reported at a seven-month high. Brent was near $92.6 before the open.
items.notes: Rupee detail comes from a headline only (seven-month high, 'past 93'); the exact level was not verified.

items.text: Mahanadi Coalfields' ₹8,981-crore IPO, an offer for sale by Coal India, was subscribed 0.49 times overall at 17:06 on Nov 20, the end of day two, per Chittorgarh. QIBs bid 1.37x, retail 0.25x, NIIs 0.18x and employees 0.09x. The grey-market premium fell to about ₹1.60, implying a listing gain of roughly 1% over the ₹136 top of the band. Bidding closes Monday, Nov 23, allotment is Nov 25 and listing is planned for Nov 27.

A Supreme Court bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi stayed the Madras High Court's findings on the Thiruparankundram hill dispute in Madurai. The High Court had allowed devotees to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon pillar near a dargah. The Supreme Court allowed a one-time lighting on Nov 24, limited to temple representatives and officials, with no public access, processions or demonstrations. It said the permission does not establish any custom, barred any construction, and said the dargah and mosque must not be disturbed. The District Collector must file a compliance report within three days of the festival. Questions under Articles 25 and 26 remain open.
items.notes: Communally sensitive dispute in Tamil Nadu. The State, HR&CE and the Dargah all opposed the HC ruling.

items.text: A two-judge Supreme Court bench including Justice Vikram Nath dismissed two Tamil Nadu applications seeking an order for Karnataka to release 11 TMC of Cauvery water, which Tamil Nadu called this year's shortfall. Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi argued that crops would suffer. Karnataka had earlier cited a rain-deficit year and drought. Justice Nath remarked orally that Tamil Nadu seemed to have plenty of money to spend on lawyers, and indicated that a third application filed that day would also fail.
items.notes: Outlook cites LiveLaw. The second judge is not named.

items.text: Opening an NIA counter-terrorism conference in New Delhi on Nov 20, Home Minister Amit Shah claimed that Kashmir is free of 'India-born' terrorists for the first time in 35 years. He made the claim after the Nov 18 killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba militant Mohd Lateef Bhat in a mosque in Zangalpora, Kulgam. Police say Bhat refused to surrender and opened fire. He was wanted for a Nov 11 attack on a CRPF post. Shah urged agencies to dismantle whole networks, not just kill individual militants, and called for stronger state ATS cyber units. He said 303 fugitives have been brought back from 36 countries since 2019.
items.notes: Shah's claim is not independently verified, and 'India-born' is undefined; foreign militants remain. PIB release title confirms Shah's congratulations (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2338078&reg=6&lang=1). Encounter details are from National Herald.

items.text: Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan dedicated India's first indigenous inactivated H5N1 bird-flu vaccine for poultry at ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal on Nov 20. It targets clade 2.3.2.1a, behind most Indian outbreaks, and is aimed first at layer and breeder flocks. The government says one dose protects for up to six months and costs ₹1–2. It will be rolled out in phases. The ministry calls it the world's first vaccine against this variant, and a ₹300-crore animal-disease laboratory was announced for Bhopal. Experts note vaccination must work alongside surveillance and culling, because vaccinated birds can carry the virus without symptoms.
items.notes: The 'world's first' claim is the ministry's. The release's claim that animal husbandry is 14% of GDP conflicts with official GVA data (about 5–6%).

items.text: Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration issued a statewide compliance order, effective immediately, tightening rules on health supplements, nutraceuticals and special dietary foods. It covers makers, importers, pharmacies, gyms and e-commerce platforms. Sellers need category-specific FSSAI licences, products cannot claim to cure or prevent disease, only Ashwagandha root may be used, and 'ORS' is banned from product names. The order follows Nov 13 inspections that found ingredients FSSAI had rejected. The FDA seized stock worth over ₹1.38 crore from 17 units and is testing sports-nutrition, weight-loss and sexual-wellness products for undeclared steroids and drugs.
items.notes: Likely syndicated copy; no FSSAI national order found for Nov 20–21.

items.text: PM Modi was scheduled to visit three states on Nov 21. In Vaishali, Bihar, he was to open or lay foundations for projects the PMO values at about ₹34,470 crore. They include Nitish Setu, a six-lane Ganga bridge between Kachchi Dargah and Bidupur meant to ease north–south Bihar traffic around Patna. He was also to address the platinum jubilee of IIT Kharagpur in West Bengal and release a commemorative coin. In Lucknow he was to attend the national skill convocation for ITI trainees, which also highlights the PM-SETU scheme for upgrading ITIs.
items.notes: Based on the advance schedule; completion of the events was not confirmed at the time of writing. No breakdown of the projects was given.

items.text: The Labour Ministry is holding a two-day Chintan Shivir in Gandhinagar on Nov 21–22 for state and UT labour, employment and industry ministers, marking one year since the four labour codes took effect. Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya chairs it, and MoS Shobha Karandlaje attends. The agenda details were not reported.
items.notes: Advance listing; no outcome yet.

items.text: Delhi's air worsened again on Nov 21. ETV Bharat, citing CPCB, says all 22 listed stations were 'very poor' in the morning, from Bawana (306) to Siri Fort (370). IANS put the city at 327 ('very poor') as the season's cold set in. Only GRAP Stages I and II are in force, after CAQM lifted Stage III on Nov 17. Falling wind speeds are expected to trap more pollution.
items.notes: ETV reports a city average of 200 at 6 am, which conflicts with its own station readings and with IANS's 327. The station data and 327 figure are used here.

items.text: A Botswana-born cheetah has given birth to four cubs, taking India's cheetah population to 62, the Environment Ministry said on Nov 20.
items.notes: Only the PIB release title was seen; the site (Kuno or Gandhi Sagar) was not confirmed.

items.text: The Health Ministry said on Nov 21 that the national HPV vaccination drive against cervical cancer has crossed 1 crore doses. The single-dose drive for adolescent girls was launched earlier in 2026.
items.notes: Only the PIB release title was seen; no state-level breakdown.
